newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Enterprises Q3 gas deliveries down.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Enterprises Q3 gas deliveries down.

text.p: Pacific Enterprises said total gas volumes delivered by Southern California Gas Co., its main subsidiary, fell during the third quarter to 224 billion cubic feet (bcf) from 237 bcf in the same 1995 period.
During the first nine months of the year, gas volumes were 644 bcf, compared with 711 bcf for the same period a year ago, the company said.
But the company noted a regional abundance of hydroelectric power experienced in prior periods was down to a more normal level in the third quarter and had less of an impact on gas sales.

Pacific Enterprises said its consolidated third quarter net income of $47 million included $51 million from SoCalGas, compared with year-ago totals of $48 million for the holding company and $47 million for the gas company.

The SoCalGas results were posted despite an authorized 1996 return on equity of 11.6 percent, down from 12 percent a year ago, along with a three percent productivity factor in operations and maintenance expenses in 1996, agreed to with the regulators under a previous settlement.

Willis Wood Jr, chairman of Pacific Enterprises said "the quarter just ended marked several key developments which enhance our future growth opportunities and provide major progress toward our goal of becoming a world-class energy company."

Wood cited the proposed merger, announced last week, between Pacific Enterprises and Enova, the parent of San Diego Gas & Electric, which, if approved by shareholders and regulators, would create a company with a market capitalization of $5.2 billion.

In addition to SoCalGas, Pacific Enterprises owns interstate and offshore natural gas pipeline operations, as well as interests in international gas distribution and domestic alternative energy operations.
SoCalGas is the nation's largest natural gas distribution utility, with more than 4.7 million customers.
